notes: This breadth set extends the six-case human-reviewed bootstrap with 12 source-grounded internal-test candidates across multiple specialties and task representations.
The 12 new candidates have AI-test Medical/References/Rights evidence, not human production review; their gold content remains development-only until explicit human semantic review.
All four grounded-teaching actions are represented: concise explanation, contrastive explanation, misconception repair and prerequisite remediation.
Representations include factual recall, clinical vignette, management decision and discrimination.
Automated structure, citation containment and verbosity checks cannot establish medical correctness.
Passing this set cannot qualify a provider for production and cannot publish any underlying content.
Visual/multimodal provider qualification remains separate until a media-bearing teaching task contract exists.

gold.canonicalExplanation: For an otherwise healthy patient undergoing elective anesthesia or sedation, ASA guidance permits clear liquids until 2 hours before the procedure.

canonicalClaims.text: Clear liquids generally require a 2-hour fasting interval before elective anesthesia or sedation in otherwise healthy patients.

requiredFacts: Clear liquids generally require at least a 2-hour fasting interval before elective anesthesia or sedation in otherwise healthy patients.
forbiddenClaims: Clear liquids require a 6-hour fasting interval in the same setting.
gold.nextPrompt: What is the clear-liquid fasting interval before elective anesthesia?

gold.canonicalExplanation: For ACS patients undergoing PCI, radial access is preferred over femoral access when feasible because it reduces bleeding and vascular complications and is associated with lower mortality.

canonicalClaims.text: For ACS PCI, radial access is preferred when feasible.
The key contrast is radial rather than femoral access because radial access reduces bleeding and vascular complications and is associated with lower mortality.

requiredFacts: Radial access is preferred over femoral access for ACS PCI when feasible.
forbiddenClaims: Femoral access is preferred over radial access for routine ACS PCI when radial access is feasible.
gold.nextPrompt: For ACS PCI, which access route is preferred when feasible, and why?

learnerError.observedBelief: Dopamine is the first-line vasopressor for most adults with septic shock.

gold.canonicalExplanation: Current Surviving Sepsis Campaign adult guidance recommends norepinephrine as the first-line vasopressor for most adults with septic shock.

canonicalClaims.text: Norepinephrine, not dopamine, is the recommended first-line vasopressor for most adults with septic shock.
When choosing the initial vasopressor in septic shock, identify norepinephrine as first-line rather than another vasopressor option.

requiredFacts: Norepinephrine is the recommended first-line vasopressor for most adults with septic shock.
forbiddenClaims: Dopamine is the first-line vasopressor for most adults with septic shock.
gold.nextPrompt: Which vasopressor should you choose first for most adults with septic shock?

gold.canonicalExplanation: Guttate psoriasis often appears in children or young adults and may follow a streptococcal upper-respiratory infection.

canonicalClaims.text: A young patient with numerous small psoriatic lesions after recent streptococcal upper-respiratory infection fits guttate psoriasis.

requiredFacts: Guttate psoriasis may follow streptococcal upper-respiratory infection in children or young adults.
forbiddenClaims: A recent streptococcal upper-respiratory infection specifically points to inverse psoriasis.
gold.nextPrompt: Which psoriasis subtype is classically associated with a recent streptococcal infection?

learnerError.selectedOptionText: IV thrombolysis is never used within 4.5 hours

gold.canonicalExplanation: For an otherwise eligible selected acute ischemic stroke patient within 4.5 hours, IV thrombolysis remains a treatment option, with alteplase or tenecteplase used in appropriate patients.

canonicalClaims.text: Eligible selected acute ischemic stroke patients presenting within 4.5 hours may receive IV thrombolysis with alteplase or tenecteplase as appropriate.

requiredFacts: IV thrombolysis remains an option for appropriately selected eligible acute ischemic stroke patients within 4.5 hours.
forbiddenClaims: IV thrombolysis is never used within 4.5 hours of acute ischemic stroke onset.
gold.nextPrompt: What reperfusion treatment remains available to an eligible selected patient within 4.5 hours?

learnerError.observedBelief: Tranexamic acid for postpartum haemorrhage should be started only after 3 hours have elapsed.

gold.canonicalExplanation: WHO recommends IV tranexamic acid for clinically diagnosed postpartum haemorrhage as early as possible and within 3 hours of birth, in addition to standard care.

canonicalClaims.text: Tranexamic acid for postpartum haemorrhage should be started as early as possible and within 3 hours of birth.
Do not wait until after 3 hours; the recommendation is early treatment within the 3-hour window.

requiredFacts: IV tranexamic acid should be started as early as possible and within 3 hours of birth for clinically diagnosed postpartum haemorrhage.
forbiddenClaims: Tranexamic acid should be started only after 3 hours have elapsed.
gold.nextPrompt: What is the timing window for IV tranexamic acid in postpartum haemorrhage?

gold.canonicalExplanation: Sudden intense eye pain with nausea, red eye and blurred vision is characteristic of acute angle-closure glaucoma and requires emergency treatment.

canonicalClaims.text: Sudden severe eye pain, nausea, redness and blurred vision should trigger recognition of acute angle-closure glaucoma.
The sudden painful red-eye syndrome is the emergency angle-closure pattern, not early open-angle glaucoma.

requiredFacts: Acute angle-closure glaucoma can present with sudden severe eye pain, nausea, red eye and blurred vision and requires emergency treatment.
forbiddenClaims: Early open-angle glaucoma is the diagnosis for this sudden painful red-eye emergency pattern.
gold.nextPrompt: Which glaucoma presentation is an ocular emergency with sudden pain, nausea and blurred vision?

learnerError.selectedOptionText: ECT is routinely the first intervention

gold.canonicalExplanation: NIMH notes that psychotherapy is often tried first for milder depression, with medication added if psychotherapy alone does not produce a good response.

canonicalClaims.text: For milder depression, psychotherapy is often tried first, with medication added if psychotherapy alone is insufficient.

requiredFacts: Psychotherapy is often tried first for milder depression, with medication added if needed.
forbiddenClaims: ECT is routinely the first intervention for milder depression.
gold.nextPrompt: What is commonly tried first for a milder form of depression?

learnerError.observedBelief: SABA-only therapy is the usual GINA Track 1 treatment at Steps 1–2 for adults and adolescents.

gold.canonicalExplanation: At GINA 2026 Track 1 Steps 1–2 for adults and adolescents, the usual treatment is as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol without scheduled maintenance dosing.

canonicalClaims.text: GINA Track 1 Steps 1–2 use as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol, not SABA-only therapy.
The Track 1 reliever contains both inhaled corticosteroid and formoterol, distinguishing it from a SABA-only regimen.

requiredFacts: GINA Track 1 Steps 1–2 use as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol for adults and adolescents.
forbiddenClaims: SABA-only therapy is the usual GINA Track 1 treatment at Steps 1–2.
gold.nextPrompt: What is the reliever treatment at GINA Track 1 Steps 1–2?

gold.canonicalExplanation: GOLD uses a post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC ratio below 0.7 as the spirometric criterion for persistent airflow obstruction compatible with COPD.

canonicalClaims.text: Before labeling persistent airflow obstruction as COPD, confirm the post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC criterion: below 0.7.
Reduced peak expiratory flow alone does not replace the post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC diagnostic criterion.

requiredFacts: A post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC below 0.7 is the GOLD spirometric criterion for persistent airflow obstruction compatible with COPD.
forbiddenClaims: Reduced peak expiratory flow alone is the required spirometric diagnostic criterion for COPD.
gold.nextPrompt: Which post-bronchodilator spirometric ratio is required for persistent airflow obstruction compatible with COPD?

gold.canonicalExplanation: For an average adult in cardiac arrest, AHA guidance recommends compressing at least 5 cm while avoiding excessive depth greater than 6 cm.

canonicalClaims.text: Adult chest compressions should reach at least 5 cm in depth.
The target is not unlimited depth: avoid compressions deeper than 6 cm, so 7–8 cm is excessive.

requiredFacts: Adult chest-compression depth should be at least 5 cm while avoiding depth greater than 6 cm.
forbiddenClaims: A depth of 7–8 cm is the recommended adult chest-compression target.
gold.nextPrompt: What adult compression-depth range should you aim for?

learnerError.observedBelief: Standard two-wavelength pulse oximetry directly measures carboxyhemoglobin accurately in carbon-monoxide poisoning.

gold.canonicalExplanation: Conventional two-wavelength pulse oximetry is not accurate when significant carboxyhemoglobin is present and may appear falsely reassuring.

canonicalClaims.text: Standard two-wavelength pulse oximetry does not accurately measure oxygenation when significant carboxyhemoglobin is present.
A reassuring conventional pulse-oximeter reading does not exclude carbon-monoxide poisoning because carboxyhemoglobin can make the reading misleading.

requiredFacts: Conventional pulse oximetry can be misleading when significant carboxyhemoglobin is present.
forbiddenClaims: Standard two-wavelength pulse oximetry directly measures carboxyhemoglobin accurately.
gold.nextPrompt: Why can a normal-looking pulse-oximeter reading be misleading in carbon-monoxide poisoning?
